Japanese prefecture population practice dataset

47 prefectures, with population counts as of October 1, 2020 and October 1,
2025. The 2025 figures are preliminary census counts as identified by the
source cited in Wikipedia. They have not been independently reconciled to
the official table.

Columns
prefecture_id: Lowercase English key created for this file, not an official code.
prefecture: English name with administrative suffixes and macrons removed.
prefecture_ja: Japanese name from the same article, useful for joining to
  official boundary data containing prefecture names such as N03_001.
population_2020: Number of people, October 1, 2020.
population_2025: Preliminary number of people, October 1, 2025.
population_change: 2025 population minus 2020 population. Negative means decline.
population_change_pct: 100 * change / 2020 population, rounded to four decimals.
  Values are percentages, not proportions. For example, 1.41 means 1.41%.
status_2025: Reminder that 2025 values are preliminary.

Suggested variable dropdown
Population in 2020
Population in 2025 (preliminary)
Population change, 2020-2025

Use the same breaks and colors for the two population counts. For change,
use fixed negative/positive intervals with a contrasting palette and a separate
zero key. The CSV contains population facts, not geographic shapes.

Page content is available under CC BY-SA 4.0.
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/
The table has been adapted by normalizing names, adding the derived key,
selecting the two population years and recalculating changes. Attribution
and transformation details accompany this copy; the package's MIT code
license does not replace source-data attribution or licensing.

The article cites this official source for the 2025 preliminary figures.
https://www.e-stat.go.jp/en/dbview?sid=0004050397

Checks
All 47 prefectures have unique English keys and Japanese names. No population
value is missing or negative. The counts reconcile to the national totals in
the same Wikipedia table (126,146,099 in 2020 and 123,049,524 in 2025).
Absolute change sums to -3,096,575 and agrees with the table's changes.

Bundled boundaries
japan_prefectures_sf.geojson contains all 47 prefectures from geoBoundaries
gbOpen JPN ADM1, boundary ID JPN-ADM1-47310658, source OpenStreetMap/Wambacher.
Boundary year represented: 2017. geoBoundaries build: December 12, 2023.
https://www.geoboundaries.org/api/current/gbOpen/JPN/ADM1/
Pinned source commit: 9469f09.
https://github.com/wmgeolab/geoBoundaries/tree/9469f09/releaseData/gbOpen/JPN/ADM1
Uses the provider's simplified GeoJSON; no further geometric simplification.
Removed the English suffix ' Prefecture', derived a lowercase prefecture_id,
retained shapeISO and rounded coordinates to six decimals in EPSG:4326.
All 47 names were checked against the population CSV. The derived key is not
an official administrative code. Islands in the supplied geometry are retained.
These older display boundaries are not a reconstruction of each census date,
and the map is not suitable for cadastral or legal boundary analysis.
